name: update_dns_record
description:
Update an existing DNS record by its numeric `record_id` (obtained from `list_dns_records`). All fields except `record_id` and `domain` are optional — pass only the ones you want to change. Idempotent: applying the same update twice is a no-op.

**Check `warnings` in the response and pass it on.** Porkbun keeps a DNS zone for every domain in the account whether or not the domain is delegated to Porkbun's nameservers, so this write succeeds either way. If the domain points somewhere else, the response is still `SUCCESS` but carries a `warnings` string naming the nameservers that actually answer — the record exists and nothing resolves differently. Do not report plain success in that case: either make the change at the provider that runs those nameservers, or offer `update_nameservers` to point the domain at Porkbun.

On this server a TXT record's content is checked before anything is sent: a DKIM key record (v=DKIM1, or p= under _domainkey) must hold a public key that parses (an RSA key of 1024 bits or more, or an ed25519 key), and an SPF record (v=spf1) must have no obvious mistake (an unknown mechanism, a bad address, a term after all, more than 10 lookups). One that fails is refused with what is wrong.

domain.description: Domain the record belongs to, e.g. `example.com`

record_id.description: Numeric record ID (as a string). Get this from `list_dns_records`.

dry_run.description: If true, validate only — confirms the record exists and is editable, returns wouldSucceed without changing it.

name: update_glue_record
description: Update the IP addresses associated with an existing glue record. Replaces the full IP list — pass all IPs you want set, not just additions. Idempotent.

domain.description: Parent domain, e.g. `example.com`

ips.description: Full replacement set of IPv4/IPv6 addresses for the host.

name: update_nameservers
description:
Replace the nameservers for a domain in the authenticated account. **This is a full replacement, not an append** — the supplied list becomes the complete set of nameservers. Most TLDs require 2-13 entries. Setting custom nameservers disables Porkbun's free DNS hosting for the domain. Idempotent: applying the same NS list twice is a no-op. The list is applied as a set — the registry may return it in a different order, so do not expect `get_nameservers` to echo your ordering back, and do not treat a reordering as drift.

On this server each name is checked for syntax first (a fully qualified host name, no duplicates), and the answer adds nameservers: { before, after }, the set the registry had and the one sent.

domain.description: Domain to update, e.g. `example.com`

nameservers.description: Full list of nameservers (e.g. `['ns1.example.com', 'ns2.example.com']`). Minimum 2, maximum 13.

dry_run.description: If true, validate only — returns wouldSucceed without changing the nameservers.

name: update_transfer_auth_code
description: Replace the authorization code on an inbound transfer that stalled because the code was wrong, and re-queue it — instead of cancelling, refunding and resubmitting. The new code is validated against the registry before being stored, so a bad one is rejected here rather than failing again days later. Only repairable transfers qualify; others return TRANSFER_NOT_REPAIRABLE. Note that a losing registrar's refusal also surfaces as a bad-auth-code status, so check for a denial notice before assuming the code is the problem.

domain.description: Domain with the stalled inbound transfer.

auth_code.description: Replacement authorization (EPP) code from the losing registrar.

dry_run.description: Validate the code without storing it or re-queueing.

name: update_webhook
description: Update a webhook endpoint. Only the supplied fields change. Set `status` to `DISABLED` to pause deliveries or `ACTIVE` to resume (resuming also clears the consecutive-failure counter). A replacement `url` must satisfy the same public-HTTPS rules as create_webhook. Idempotent. Calls the Porkbun Webhooks API (https://porkbun.com/llms/webhooks).

url.description: New HTTPS URL. Same rules as create_webhook: port 443, publicly resolvable hostname, no embedded credentials.

events.description: Replacement event subscription list (or `['*']` for all).
